description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a universally adored Indian curry renowned for its luxurious, creamy tomato-based sauce and succulent pieces of marinated chicken. This iconic dish delivers a perfect harmony of smoky, tangy, and subtly sweet flavors, making it an incredibly comforting and satisfying meal. It is a true staple of Indian cuisine, ideal for a memorable lunch or dinner.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in hot water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, 1 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and salt. Mix well to ensure all chicken pieces are coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for deeper flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Sear the chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until lightly browned. The chicken does not need to be cooked through at this stage. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another 1 tablespoon of butter. Once melted, add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Saute for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews, cumin powder, coriander powder, and 1 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder. Add sugar and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the mixture has thickened slightly.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain the Gravy
instructions.text: Remove the whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaf). Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky texture, pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan, pressing down on any solids. Discard the solids.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish the Curry
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken to the smooth gravy. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter and stir until melted and incorporated. Pour in the heavy cream and gently stir. If using, crush the fenugreek leaves between your palms and add them to the curry. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to cook through. Adjust salt and sugar to taste.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve your authentic Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani hot with basmati rice, naan bread, or roti for a delightful Indian lunch.

tips: For truly tender chicken, marinate it overnight. The yogurt helps to tenderize the meat beautifully.
Do not skip blending and straining the gravy. This step is crucial for achieving the signature silky smooth texture of authentic Butter Chicken.
Always finish with a knob of butter and a swirl of cream just before serving. This adds richness and a beautiful sheen to the curry, enhancing its classic taste.
article:
Unlock the secrets to a beloved Indian culinary masterpiece with our guide to making the ultimate Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani. This iconic dish, known for its velvety texture and rich, aromatic flavors, is a staple in Indian cuisine and a fantastic choice for a comforting and satisfying lunch. Forget bland takeout; we’re diving deep into crafting this restaurant-quality dish right in your own kitchen, transforming your midday meal into an extraordinary feast. Get ready to impress your taste buds and those of your loved ones with this truly special Indian lunch recipe.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani as it's traditionally known, is a quintessential Indian curry that originated in Delhi in the 1950s. It was first created by Kundan Lal Gujral at Moti Mahal restaurant, and its popularity quickly spread across India and then the world. The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter," perfectly describing the dish's indulgent nature. At its heart, Butter Chicken features tender pieces of marinated chicken, often grilled or pan-fried, swimming in a luxurious, creamy tomato-based sauce. This sauce is a symphony of flavors, combining sweet tomatoes, rich cream, fragrant spices like garam masala, cumin, coriander, and a hint of fenugreek (kasoori methi) for that unmistakable authentic taste. It’s famous for its mild heat, making it accessible to most palates, and its incredibly smooth, melt-in-your-mouth texture, making it a perfect, comforting Indian lunch recipe.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting authentic Butter Chicken requires a few key components, divided into the chicken marinade and the luscious sauce. Quality ingredients are paramount for the best results.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
*   1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

For the Murgh Makhani Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter (or ghee)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes or 3-4 fresh large tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup cashew nuts, soaked in hot water for 15 minutes (for thickening)
*   1/2 cup water (or chicken broth)
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or half-and-half)
*   1-2 teaspoons sugar (to balance acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making delicious Butter Chicken at home is a rewarding process. Follow these steps for a perfect Indian lunch:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, for maximum flavor.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat a little oil or butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until nicely browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Cashew Paste:** While the chicken cooks, drain the soaked cashews and blend them with a couple of tablespoons of water until you get a smooth, thick paste. Set aside.
4.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In the same pan (or a separate pot), melt the butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until they turn translucent and slightly golden, about 8-10 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
5.  **Build the Sauce Base:** Stir in the crushed tomatoes or tomato puree. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have darkened slightly and the oil begins to separate from the edges. This step is crucial for depth of flavor.
6.  **Add Spices and Cashew Paste:** Reduce the heat to low. Stir in the red chili powder, cumin, coriander, and garam masala. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, to toast the spices. Immediately add the cashew paste and water (or broth). Stir well to combine.
7.  **Simmer and Blend:** Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Remove from heat and, using an immersion blender or by carefully transferring to a regular blender, blend the sauce until completely smooth. Pass it through a fine-mesh sieve for an ultra-velvety texture, if desired.
8.  **Finish the Butter Chicken:** Return the smooth sauce to the pot over low heat. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces, kasoori methi, heavy cream, and sugar. Simmer gently for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the sauce’s flavors. Taste and adjust salt or sugar if needed.
9.  **Garnish and Serve:** Ladle the rich Butter Chicken into serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and an extra swirl of cream, if desired.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Butter Chicken is all about attention to detail.

*   **Marination Time is Key:** Don't skimp on marinating the chicken. The longer it marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Sear, Don't Overcook:** When cooking the chicken, sear it quickly to get a nice brown crust, but don't cook it all the way through. It will finish cooking in the sauce, preventing it from drying out.
*   **Blend for Smoothness:** For an incredibly silky sauce, blending the cooked sauce base until absolutely smooth is essential. Passing it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending will remove any remaining fibrous bits from onions or tomatoes, giving you that luxurious, restaurant-style texture.
*   **Kasoori Methi Magic:** Don't skip the kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves). Crush them between your palms before adding to release their unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is characteristic of authentic Butter Chicken.
*   **Balance Flavors:** The sugar in the recipe isn't just for sweetness; it balances the acidity of the tomatoes. Taste and adjust as needed, as tomato acidity can vary. A pinch more sugar can transform the sauce.
*   **Use Quality Butter and Cream:** Since "butter" is in the name, using good quality unsalted butter and heavy cream will significantly impact the richness and flavor of your Murgh Makhani.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a hearty and satisfying dish on its own, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments. For an authentic Indian lunch experience:

*   **Naan Bread:** Warm, fluffy naan is perfect for scooping up every last bit of the creamy sauce. Garlic naan or butter naan are particularly delightful choices.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice provides a neutral base that soaks up the rich flavors beautifully. A sprinkle of fresh cilantro over the rice adds a touch of freshness.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber or mint raita (yogurt dip) offers a refreshing contrast to the richness of the curry.
*   **Salad:** A simple side salad with thinly sliced red onions and a squeeze of lemon juice can add a fresh crunch.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is undeniably delicious, there are several ways to adapt the recipe to suit different preferences or dietary needs:

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan Butter "Chicken":** Substitute the chicken with paneer (Indian cheese), tofu, or even chickpeas. For a vegan version, use plant-based yogurt, coconut cream instead of heavy cream, and vegan butter or oil.
*   **Spice Level:** If you prefer more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili during the onion sautéing stage. For a milder version, reduce the chili powder.
*   **Healthier Options:** For a lighter take, use chicken breast and reduce the amount of butter and cream. You can also substitute some of the heavy cream with milk or light coconut milk, though it will alter the richness slightly.
*   **Different Proteins:** While chicken is traditional, you can experiment with lamb or even shrimp, adjusting cooking times accordingly.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** For an extra layer of flavor, after cooking the chicken, you can perform a "dhungar" or smoke infusion. Place a small, hot charcoal in a small metal bowl in the center of the chicken and sauce, drizzle a little ghee over it, and quickly cover the pot for a few minutes.

Bringing this glorious Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani to your table is a culinary triumph that promises to delight. Its rich history, complex yet comforting flavors, and velvety texture make it an unparalleled choice for an Indian lunch. With our comprehensive guide, you're now equipped to create a dish that not only satisfies your hunger but also transports you to the vibrant streets of India with every delicious bite. Enjoy the journey of making and savoring this magnificent creation!
